reason: Direct main comparison and witnesses601–603 establish the exact source hypotheses. In7.18.1 C consists of integral k-algebras with flat homomorphisms and F:C→Ens commutes filtered inductive limits. In7.18.2 the printed cases are(a) k separably closed and K/k separable,(b) k infinite and K/k pure; its conclusion is injectivity. The proof uses F(A→k), but evaluation k[t]→k at t=0 is not flat: tensoring the injective multiplication-by-t map on k[t] gives the zero map on nonzero k. Here is a concrete counterexample on exactly the printed category. Fix algebraically closed k and define G(A)=Z when Frac(A)/k is algebraic and G(A)=0 otherwise. Every flat map of nonzero domains A→B is injective: for nonzero a in A, flatness preserves the injection A --a→ A after tensoring with B; if a mapped to0, the resulting zero map B→B would be injective, forcing B=0. Hence Frac(A) injects into Frac(B), so transcendence over k cannot disappear. Define G on arrows by identity when both values are Z and by the unique map whenever the target is0. There is no arrow from the transcendental case to the algebraic case; these maps compose exactly, so G is a functor. A filtered diagram of these injections has an integral colimit. Every fraction in the colimit comes from a stage. If every stage fraction field is algebraic over k, every such fraction is algebraic, so G(colim A_i)=Z=colim G(A_i). If some stage contains a transcendental element, it remains transcendental in all later stages; the stages receiving that stage are cofinal and G is0 there, so both sides are0. Thus G commutes the required filtered limits. Now K=k(t) satisfies both printed cases(a) and(b), but G(k)→G(K) is Z→0, which is not injective. For the exact set-valued version one may replace Z and0 by a fixed two-element set and a singleton, with the same identity/collapse maps and the same colimit calculation. In7.18.3 the additional norm hypothesis is that F(k)→F(k′)→F(k) is multiplication by[k′:k] for each finite extension k′/k. Since k is algebraically closed, every such extension has degree1, and choosing the identity norm for G satisfies this hypothesis. Its kernel Z for K=k(t) is not torsion, and its map is not injective, refuting both printed conclusions(i),(ii) on592. Finally7.18.4 assumes surjectivity for the coordinate ring A of every nonempty affine open U⊂A_k^n. For n>0, Frac(A)=k(T_1,…,T_n), so G(k)→G(A) is Z→0 and is surjective; for n=0 it is id_Z. Thus the added assumption holds, k is infinite, and the norm hypothesis also holds, yet Z→0 is not bijective. This refutes its final bijectivity conclusion, not its surjectivity conclusion. The specific K_• functor in7.18.5 has additional finite-Tor pullbacks (the printed citation IV2.12), not supplied for arbitrary F in7.18.1; the present counterexample does not refute those specific K_• conclusions. No corrected general theorem or new hypothesis is inserted. Final editorial disposition: retain the author wording and publish this demonstrated limitation in the decision dossier and edition preface. This closes the choice of reading; it does not claim that the source assertion has been repaired.
